subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In a 2019 study, researchers Dr. Layla Hassan and Dr. Olivia Brooks wanted to explore the effects of cold stratification on the germination of Echinacea purpurea seeds in North America.
• The team of researchers tested 150 Echinacea purpurea seeds that had undergone cold stratification treatment.
• Of these, 117 seeds (78%) germinated.
• As a control, Dr. Hassan and Dr. Brooks tested 150 Echinacea purpurea seeds that had not undergone cold stratification treatment.
• Of these, 98 seeds (65%) germinated.
prompt: The student wants to describe the study's research methodology. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Dr. Hassan and Dr. Brooks wanted to explore the effects of cold stratification on Echinacea purpurea seed germination.
choices.B: In the study, a higher percentage of Echinacea purpurea seeds that underwent cold stratification germinated than those that had not undergone the treatment.
choices.C: Research by Dr. Hassan and Dr. Brooks revealed that 117 of 150—that is, 78%—of the Echinacea purpurea seeds that had undergone cold stratification germinated.
choices.D: The team of researchers tested the germination of 150 Echinacea purpurea seeds that had undergone cold stratification treatment and 150 Echinacea purpurea seeds that had not undergone the treatment.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it directly describes the study's research methodology by explaining the experimental design and procedures. The sentence specifies that the researchers tested two groups of 150 seeds each—one group that received cold stratification treatment and one control group that did not. This description of the experimental setup, including sample sizes and the presence of both treatment and control conditions, is precisely what defines research methodology: how the study was conducted rather than why it was conducted or what results were found.
